newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES FIRMER IN TIGHT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET RATES FIRMER IN TIGHT MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened short of cash on Tuesday with short-term trading rates quoted up from Monday's levels, dealers said.

"The market is very tight at the moment and rates have gone up," a dealer said, adding this was likely to be the case until Thursday, when a number of maturing treasury bills were expected to restore liquidity to the system.

Dealers said a recent announcement by the central Reserve Bank that it was raising to 20 percent from 17.5 percent its statutory reserve requirement ratio on all deposit liabilities of commercial and merchant banks would only have a temporary upward effect on trading rates on the local money market.
"Obviously the cost of funds for banks will be higher and the money they have to invest will be less," said one.
"But we don't expect it to affect the local market for long because the market will be very flush from around 15 December on maturity of a lot of treasury bills," he added.

Meanwhile on Tuesday morning, discount houses were selling treasury bills into the market at 19 percent, up from 18.75 percent the previous day. NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were also quoted firmer at 24 percent (buying) and 20 percent (selling), up from 19.75 and 19.25 percent, while bankers acceptances were being bought and sold at 22 and 19 percent respectively from 19.50 and 19 percent.
Call money went up to 24 percent from 18.50 percent in a market which was Z$167.4 million in deficit at settlement. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9--
